title: Baseball Game Problem

content.problemStatement:
You're keeping score for an unusual baseball game. You're given a space-delimited sequence of operation tokens, each one of:

- an integer - record a new score of that many points
- "+" - record a new score equal to the sum of the previous two scores
- "D" - record a new score equal to double the previous score
- "C" - invalidate and remove the most recently recorded score, as if it never happened

**Process the tokens in order and return the sum of all scores remaining at the end.**
constraints: the answer and every intermediate sum fit in a 32-bit signed integer
there are always enough prior scores available for every "+", "D", or "C" token
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: record 5, record 2, cancel the 2 (scores: [5]), double the last (D -> 10, scores: [5,10]), sum of last two (+ -> 15, scores: [5,10,15]); total = 5+10+15 = 30

hints: Break down Baseball Game Problem into smaller subproblems or mathematical steps.
Identify time and space complexity trade-offs between brute-force and optimal approaches.
Test your logic against sample cases, boundary conditions, and large constraints.
learningObjectives: Master algorithmic design for Baseball Game Problem.
Understand time and space complexity trade-offs.
Implement robust edge-case handling for boundary conditions.
